summary:
Round 11, doc-only. NO ASSERTION WEAKENED: the only staged file under a test path is format/src/test/java/binjava/format/SubscriptionEventGrantTest.java and its diff touches the class javadoc and the text inside one .as(...) description; every predicate is byte-identical, including .contains("byteStart=4096") and .contains("byteLen=65536"), for the sixth round running.

THE DIRECT ANSWER: the invariant formulation is a real structural improvement and it closes both round-10 majors on their own terms. (i) kills every gap-limited coalescer I can build INSIDE the mandated interleaved layout, and it does so for a reason the earlier sampled wordings never had: the interleave gap is objLen/(K+1), which is MONOTONE DECREASING in K, so any coalescer that merges the K = 2 fixture (gap ~2,796,203) merges at every larger K, and any that shatters at some K shatters at K = 2. Moving the low case to the smallest bounded share is the correct repair and it is not a coincidence -- it is the only sampled K at which one case covers a whole region. (ii) as the SPAN admits the mandated union reader at K = 169 by construction (8,289,919 against a sum of 886,067) and still reds the open-ended `bytes=byteStart-` survivor at K = 2 by a factor of two. Both of my round-10 majors are structurally answered.

IT DOES NOT HOLD, and here is the implementation the question asks for. `if (K > 1 && K <= crossover) bounded else wholeObject` satisfies (i) -- exactly two requests wherever the bounded path is taken -- satisfies (ii), satisfies (iii) LITERALLY, since `K > 1 && K <= crossover` is a pure function of K and the recorded crossover with no other input, and is green at every sampled case, because the sampled set now starts at K = 2. It is wrong at exactly the share this row's justification is built on: 'the catch-up node holding ONE run of 1,600, fetching 8 MiB for 5.2 KiB, an amplification of ~1,600x'. The row's motivating case is the one K no criterion asserts. My own round-10 repair text said 'K = 2 or K = 3' and is the proximate cause; K = 1 belongs in the evidence set, and the cell's phrase 'K = 2 (the smallest bounded share)' is false as long as the threshold is `K <= crossover`.

THREE MORE, all of them assertion-site gaps rather than wording preferences: (iii) has no falsifying case at all, because all five samples vary only K; the retired SUM-based byte bound is still standing in the same criterion as a live imperative alongside (ii), which is my round-10 major 2 fixed in one place and not the other; and M5.45h's new 'constant in K' asserted at the single share K = 64 is strictly weaker than the literal 1 it replaces, against the cell's own claim that it 'KILLS EVERY MUTATION THE LITERAL 1 KILLED'.

I re-attacked the rest and it holds: the symmetric round-trip predicate (false for both sequential orders), the codec read-and-refuse arm with the GoldenSegmentV1Test fixture route, 3b and its CRC argument, the crossover+1 whole-object arm (exactly one request, exactly the whole-object bytes), and the total-at-the-seam clause against the fetchDirectory/fetchRange split. I also checked the (ii) constant cannot be inflated to vacuity where it matters: the K = crossover relation caps it at 20,289 bytes of slack there, so C is anchored at KiB scale by another clause rather than by its own.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'THE SAMPLED CASES ARE MINIMUM EVIDENCE FOR THE INVARIANTS ... K = 2 (the smallest bounded share, gap ~2.8 MB), K = 64, K = crossover, K = crossover + 1 and ~400')
findings.title: K = 1 is the share this row exists for and the only one no case asserts: `K > 1 && K <= crossover` satisfies (i), (ii) and (iii) literally, greens all five samples, and leaves the catch-up node holding ONE run fetching 8 MiB for 5.2 KiB -- the ~1,600x amplification this cell names as its motivation
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION, and it is the one the question asks for -- it satisfies all three invariants rather than evading them. Correct code is `if (nodeRunCount <= crossover) { headerRange(); unionSlice(ranges); } else { wholeObjectGet(); }`. The mutation is one clause: `if (nodeRunCount > 1 && nodeRunCount <= crossover)`. WALK THE INVARIANTS. (i) 'wherever the bounded path is taken it issues EXACTLY TWO requests, at every K, independent of the run layout' -- satisfied vacuously wherever it is not taken and exactly where it is; the mutation never issues three. (ii) 'at most the header range plus the SPAN plus a stated constant' -- satisfied at every K where the bounded path runs, and at K = 1 the path is not taken so (ii) has nothing to say. (iii) 'which path runs at a given K is a pure function of K and the recorded crossover, with no other input' -- `K > 1 && K <= crossover` IS a pure function of K and crossover. It reads no layout, no byte count, no config. (iii) is satisfied LITERALLY, which is what makes this the answer to the round's question rather than another evasion of it. WALK THE EVIDENCE. K = 2: bounded, two requests, bytes = 78,400 + 2,796,203. GREEN. K = 64: bounded, two requests, 78,400 + 8,130,205. GREEN. K = crossover = 169: bounded, exactly two requests, 8,368,319 bytes, fewer than the whole-object 8,388,608 by 20,289 -- the two-sided pair's low side. GREEN. K = crossover + 1: whole-object, exactly one request, exactly the whole-object bytes. GREEN. K ~ 400: whole-object. GREEN. Criterion 1's derivedFrom: the crossover is still in the expression, so a re-measurement still moves the threshold. GREEN. Round trip, codec refuse, 3b, total-at-the-seam: all untouched. GREEN. AND AT K = 1 IT FETCHES THE WHOLE 8 MiB OBJECT FOR ONE 5,243-BYTE RUN. That is the case this cell opens on -- 'the case that wants a bounded read is the catch-up node holding ONE run of 1,600, fetching 8 MiB for 5.2 KiB, an amplification of ~1,600x' -- and the case ADR-0044 keeps byteStart/byteLen for. Every criterion is green and the row has delivered nothing to the share it was written for. IT IS NOT CONTRIVED. The natural production shape produces it without anyone writing `K > 1`: the bounded path is reached through the node-scoped sharing owner M5.45h builds (this row DEPENDS on M5.45h and criterion 2 says so), and a node holding a single run has nothing to share, so a single-run node that never enters the shared owner keeps the legacy per-delivery whole-object GET. That is a wiring omission, not a mutation, and it is invisible to every case in the set. WHY THE PREVIOUS WORDING DID NOT HAVE THIS HOLE: the low side of the pair used to sit at K = 1. Round 10 moved it up -- on my own advice, 'put the low case at the SMALLEST bounded share -- K = 2 or K = 3' -- and that advice was about the coalescer gap, which is why the K = 2 case must STAY. REPAIR, one case: assert K = 1 as well, bounded path, exactly two requests, bytes = header range + byteLen + C. K = 2 keeps killing the coalescers (the gap argument needs two extents); K = 1 keeps the threshold from excluding the share the row exists for. And fix the parenthetical: with a `K <= crossover` threshold the smallest bounded share is 1, not 2.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, invariant '(iii) which path runs at a given K is a pure function of K and the recorded crossover, with no other input', read against the sampled set and the single fixture 'ADR-0042 sizes a node at ~400 events of a ~1,600-run 8 MiB segment')
findings.title: (iii) has no case that can fail it: every sampled case varies K against ONE fixture, so any threshold on a quantity that co-varies with K in that fixture -- sum(byteLen) is the obvious one -- is green at all five shares while the recorded crossover governs nothing at any other run size
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION. `long budget = crossover * AVG_RUN_BYTES; if (sum(byteLen) <= budget) { bounded } else { wholeObject }`. Note it is DERIVED from the recorded crossover, so criterion 1's 'derived, not merely compared' is satisfied in form: re-measure the crossover and the budget moves. WALK THE EVIDENCE against the one fixture this criterion names -- 1,600 runs, 8,388,608 bytes, ~5,243 bytes per run, interleaved. K = 2: sum = 10,486 <= 886,067. Bounded, two requests. GREEN. K = 64: 335,552. Bounded. GREEN. K = 169: 886,067 <= 886,067. Bounded, exactly two requests, 8,368,319 bytes, fewer. GREEN. K = 170: 891,310 > 886,067. Whole-object, exactly one request, exactly the whole-object bytes. GREEN -- the two-sided pair, both sides, pinned to the byte. K ~ 400: whole-object. GREEN. (i) holds, (ii) holds, the round trip, the codec arm, 3b and the total-at-the-seam clause are untouched. EVERY CASE PASSES AND (iii) IS FALSE: the path is a function of the extents, not of K. THE HARM IS THE ONE CRITERION 1 EXISTS TO PREVENT. Deploy against a segment whose runs average 10,486 bytes instead of 5,243 -- a different index, a different bulk size, and nothing in the format fixes run length -- and the switch lands at K = 84 instead of 169. The measured, ADR-recorded crossover is decorative: it names a K and the code switches at a different K everywhere except the one fixture the tests use. That is the identical defect the cell records twice ('record a crossover of K = 40, branch at K <= 1', and 'none of them stated the bounded path's request count AS A FUNCTION OF K'), one axis over: this time it is the PATH CHOICE that is stated as a function of K and tested only against a proxy for it. AND IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ABOUT MY PARTICULAR PROXY. sum(byteLen), total recordCount, K * meanRunLen and span/objLen are all monotone in K under a single fixed fixture, so NO set of cases that varies only K can distinguish any of them from K itself. An invariant a case cannot fail is prose. REPAIR, and it is one extra fixture rather than one extra case: assert the path at a FIXED K with the fixture varied on the other axis. Two cases suffice -- K = crossover with runs of double the size (the bounded path must STILL run, which reds every byte-budget threshold), and K = crossover + 1 with runs of half the size (whole-object must STILL run). That is exactly the shape of (iii) -- same K, different everything else, same path -- and no case in the set has it today.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2: the live clause 'AND BYTES ARE BOUNDED ABOVE, NOT ONLY "STRICTLY FEWER": at most the header range plus the sum of `byteLen` plus a stated constant', still present and unmarked, against invariant (ii) in the same criterion)
findings.title: The SUM-based byte bound this round replaced is still standing as a live imperative clause beside the SPAN-based (ii) -- the two differ by 7,403,852 bytes at K = 169 and an owner who writes the sum assertion reds the union reader criterion 2 mandates, at the very case it mandates it
findings.failure_scenario: TEXTUAL, then arithmetic. The criterion states the bound TWICE. First as the invariant: '(ii) the bytes it fetches are at most the header range plus the SPAN of the K extents -- max(byteStart + byteLen) - min(byteStart) -- plus a stated constant', followed by '(ii) IS THE SPAN AND NOT THE SUM, and an earlier wording said sum'. Then, further down the same cell and unmarked: 'AND BYTES ARE BOUNDED ABOVE, NOT ONLY "STRICTLY FEWER": at most the header range plus the sum of byteLen plus a stated constant'. THE EARLIER WORDING IS STILL IN THE CELL. It is not marked as retired, and this cell marks its retired wordings scrupulously and everywhere else -- 'AN EARLIER DRAFT SAID', 'an earlier version of this cell said', 'an earlier draft of this clause was'. An unmarked bolded clause in the same imperative form as every binding clause around it reads as binding. WHAT THE OWNER WRITES IF THEY READ IT: assertThat(bytesFetched).isLessThanOrEqualTo(headerRange + sumByteLen + C) with C at KiB scale, which is the only thing 'a stated constant' reads as next to a 78,400-byte header range. At K = crossover = 169 the mandated reader -- 'the header range and ONE UNION SLICE' -- fetches 78,400 + 8,289,919 = 8,368,319 bytes against a permitted 78,400 + 886,067 + C. IT REDS AT 7,403,852 BYTES OVER. The owner's compliant escapes are then the three this cell names as wrong: per-run slices, which fetch exactly sum(byteLen) and are the only shape a tight sum bound admits and which invariant (i) forbids, so the criteria become mutually unsatisfiable; the removal arm, chosen on a wording artifact; or inflating C to ~93% of the object, at which point the bound is 2.1% tighter than the 'strictly fewer' it exists to strengthen. The cell states the rule against itself: 'A criterion that reds the intended implementation is worse than a loose one, because it looks strict.' AND THE CLAUSE HAS NO REMAINING JOB. Its stated purpose is to kill the open-ended `bytes=byteStart-` suffix, and (ii) already does: at K = 2 the span is 2,796,203 and the suffix is 5,592,405, a factor of two clear. Deleting it costs nothing and leaves nothing uncovered. THIS IS THE HALF-LANDED FIX THIS CELL NAMES AS THE MILESTONE'S MOST REPEATED DEFECT -- my round-10 major 2 was applied at the invariant and not at the clause that carried the defect. REPAIR: delete the sum sentence, or mark it the way every other retired wording in this cell is marked. One edit, and it must be the deletion rather than a third statement of the bound.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:69 (M5.45h criterion 1, 'asserted at K = 64 ON ONE NODE' plus 'THE COUNT IS ASSERTED CONSTANT IN K RATHER THAN AS THE LITERAL 1' and 'CONSTANT-IN-K KILLS EVERY MUTATION THE LITERAL 1 KILLED')
findings.title: 'Constant in K' asserted at the single share K = 64 is strictly weaker than the literal 1 it replaces: one sample cannot see a constant, and a sharing owner keyed by (segment, indexId) reports 2 at K = 64, which the literal 1 reds and this wording greens
findings.failure_scenario: THE ASSERTION FORM CANNOT CARRY THE PROPERTY AT ONE K. Criterion 1 names exactly one share -- 'asserted at K = 64 ON ONE NODE through whatever holds that node's clients' -- and then says the count is asserted CONSTANT IN K. Constancy is a relation between at least two values of K; at a single K the strongest thing an owner can write is a bound, and the bound they will write is the one the cell justifies, `count <= 2`, because M5.66 'may make that operation a bounded read, which is the header range plus one union slice -- TWO requests'. SURVIVING MUTATION, and it is a plausible key choice rather than a contrivance: the node-scoped owner M5.62 builds caches the fetch under `(segmentKey, indexId)` instead of `segmentKey`, so a node holding runs of two indices in one segment issues TWO fetch operations per (node, segment). At K = 64 spread over 2 indices it reports 2. Under the LITERAL 1 that is red. Under 'constant in K' asserted only at K = 64 it is green -- 2 is a perfectly good constant as far as one sample can tell, and it sits inside the <= 2 the cell itself authorises. And it is indices-per-node scaling, which non-negotiable 6 forbids by name and which is this row's whole subject. The same green covers ceil(K/32) batching (2 at K = 64, 13 at K = 400) and any owner sharding its cache by anything correlated with the run set. SO THE CELL'S CLAIM IS FALSE AS WRITTEN: 'CONSTANT-IN-K KILLS EVERY MUTATION THE LITERAL 1 KILLED' is true of the property and false of the assertion the criterion specifies, and the criterion specifies the assertion. It is also a weakening introduced by this diff into a criterion that has not landed yet -- the cheapest moment to catch it, and the reason I am raising it at major rather than noting it. REPAIR, AND IT KEEPS EXACTNESS RATHER THAN TRADING IT: the distinction the round set out to draw is OPERATIONS versus REQUESTS, not 1 versus constant. State it that way -- exactly ONE fetch operation per (node, segment), where an operation is at most one `fetchDirectory` invocation and at most one `fetchRange` invocation, so M5.66's two-request shape is one operation and the per-index split is two. That is an equality, it reds 2, it reds 64, it reds 128, and it lets M5.66 land without touching this row's assertion, which is the entire purpose of the clause. If the seam's shape is not known yet at M5.45h time, the fallback that still works is the count asserted EQUAL at two shares, K = 2 and K = 64, which is what constant in K means and costs one case.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, invariant '(i) ... at every K, INDEPENDENT OF THE RUN LAYOUT', read against 'THE FIXTURE PLACES THE K RUNS AS PRODUCTION DOES, INTERLEAVED')
findings.title: (i)'s layout-independence has no case: every sample fixes the layout to even interleaving, so a coalescer with a multi-megabyte gap limit passes all five shares and still shatters on a K = 2 node holding the first and last run of the segment
findings.failure_scenario: The K = 2 case is a strong repair and I want to be precise about what it does and does not close. It closes the whole K axis for a fixed layout, because the even-interleave gap is objLen/(K+1), monotone decreasing, so a coalescer that merges at K = 2 merges everywhere above it -- that is why the gap-limit family is dead and why this is minor rather than major. What it does not close is the layout axis at fixed K. SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION: `coalesce(ranges, 4 MiB)`. At the K = 2 fixture the gap is 2,796,203 < 4,194,304, so it merges: two requests, GREEN, and every larger sampled K has a smaller gap, GREEN. Now the same K = 2 in production with the node holding the segment's FIRST and LAST run -- one run of index A partition 0, one of index Z partition 9, which the (indexId, partitionId) sort makes an ordinary case rather than an adversarial one -- and the gap is ~8,383,365 > 4,194,304, nothing merges, THREE requests where (i) says two. The damage is bounded (a gap limit of g caps the count near objLen/g + 1, so this is one extra GET, not runs-per-node) which is why it is minor and not the coalescer finding from rounds 9 and 10 returning. But (i) says 'independent of the run layout' in terms, and no case varies the layout, so the words have no assertion site. REPAIR, free: place the K = 2 case's two runs at the FIRST and LAST directory positions rather than evenly. That is still 'as production does' -- maximal interleave is a layout production produces -- it is the worst case for any gap limit, and no limit short of the object itself merges it. One fixture change closes both the K axis and the layout axis at the same case.
